description: Dated staged construction on the author-approved CAD reference shape

sources.use: Actual upper-bench height is 6 m; bench interface is 6 m below the inner crown.
Calendar dates, observed targets, three chord depths and monitoring histories; original images checked on 2026-09-23
Actual changed support for 935--915: 29 cm C30 early-strength concrete, I22b at 0.6 m, 5 m bolts; 40 cm lining; combined equivalent pre-secondary-lining support stiffness 3.82 MPa/m
Corroborates actual changed support, 29 cm shotcrete and 40 cm invert. Table 6.11 stiffness 11.2 MPa/m is a theoretical demand/design quantity, not a measured installed stiffness.

interpretation.time: Event days are exact calendar-date differences. Raw digitized within-day coordinates are retained as graphical abscissae, never reported as observed hours.
interpretation.bench: The author-confirmed 6 m upper-bench height fixes the excavation interface; it is not an inverse parameter.
interpretation.support: EA = 3.82 MPa/m times (4.9 m)^2; EI = EA times (0.29 m)^2 / 12. This effective bonded frame represents the damaged composite support response, not an intact C30 material modulus. Half and twice this stiffness are evaluated without fitting it.
interpretation.installation: Upper arch installed at the assumed first-reading age, lower walls 0.5 day after lower-bench passage, invert initial support on the recorded closure date. Each segment is stress free at installation and shares rotations with installed segments.
interpretation.casting: Only the invert arc gains a 40 cm bonded concrete frame at casting, assuming E=30 GPa and nu=0.2. No unrecorded wall lining or full secondary ring is activated. Omission of this addition tests its influence.
interpretation.geometry: Existing CAD shape and actual target mapping retained. Bench removal is represented by delayed lower-wall confinement release on the final boundary; an interior retained-bench mesh and excavation floor are not resolved.
interpretation.weights: All original 935/915 observations and channel noise scales retained; one constant offset per channel is profiled, with that channel's own first record as its mechanical datum.
